style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>any condition established in the </div><div id="a16037" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>upon, the total commitment amounts do not necessarily </div><div id="a16113" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:92px;">party.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px;white-space:pre"> </div>The credit risk involved in issuing letters of In </div><div id="a16208" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:107px;">general, management does not anticipate any material losses as a result<div </div>MEASUREMENTS</div><div id="a16686" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:31px;">The fair value of an asset or liability is the price that would be received to sell </div>In estimating fair value, the Company utilizes valuation techniques that are consistent with<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>the market approach, the income </div><div id="a16693" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:77px;">approach and/or the cost approach.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>Such valuation techniques are consistently applied.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px;white-space:pre"> </div>Inputs to valuation techniques include the </div><div id="a16695" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:92px;">assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>to quoted prices in active markets for identical </div><div id="a16707" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:4px;top:123px;">assets or liabilities and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px;white-space:pre"> </div>The fair value hierarchy is as follows: </div></div></div></ix:nonNumeric></div></div>

These might<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>for identical </div><div id="a16737" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:40px;top:70px;">or similar assets or Roman';left:40px;top:101px;">corroborated, by market data by correlation or other means</div><div id="a16742" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:355px;top:101px;">.</div><div id="a16745" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:16px;top:125px;">&#9679;</div><div id="a16747" Roman';left:48px;top:538px;">31, 2025.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div></div><div id="a24847" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:569px;">We continue<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>to closely monitor our cost of deposits and deposit mix as we manage through the current rate<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>environment. </div><div id="a24850" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:48px;top:600px;">MARKET RISK AND INTEREST RATE<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>SENSITIVITY</div><div id="a24853" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;left:48px;top:630px;">Market Risk and Interest Rate Sensitivity </div><div id="a24856" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:48px;top:661px;">Overview.</div><div id="a24857" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:102px;top:661px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div></div><div id="a24858" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:109px;top:661px;">Market risk arises from changes in interest rates, exchange rates,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>commodity prices, and equity prices.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>We have risk </div><div id="a24861" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:676px;">management policies designed to monitor and limit exposure to market<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>risk and we do not participate in activities that give rise to </div><div id="a24863" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:692px;">significant market risk involving exchange rates, commodity prices, or<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>equity prices.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>In asset and liability management activities, our </div><div id="a24866" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:707px;">policies are designed to minimize structural interest rate risk.</div><div id="a24869" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:48px;top:738px;">Interest Rate Risk Management.</div><div id="a24870" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:219px;top:738px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div></div><div id="a24871" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:226px;top:738px;">Our net income is largely dependent on net interest income.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px;white-space:pre"> </div>Net interest income is susceptible to </div><div id="a24874" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:753px;">interest rate risk to the degree that interest-bearing liabilities mature<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>or reprice on a different basis than interest-earning assets.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px;white-space:pre"> </div>When </div><div id="a24881" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:768px;">interest-bearing liabilities mature or reprice more quickly<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>than interest-earning assets in a given period, a significant increase in </div><div id="a24886" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:784px;">market rates of interest could adversely affect net interest<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>income.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>Similarly, when interest-earning<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>assets mature or reprice more </div><div id="a24891" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:799px;">quickly than interest-bearing liabilities, falling market interest rates could<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>result in a decrease in net interest income.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>Net interest </div><div id="a24896" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:814px;">income is also affected by changes in the portion of interest-earning<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>assets that are funded by interest-bearing liabilities rather than by </div><div id="a24901" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:830px;">other sources of funds, such as noninterest-bearing deposits and shareowners&#8217;<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>equity. <div id="a24907" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:14.72px;left:401px;top:992px;">44 </div><div id="a24909" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:49px;">We have established<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>what we believe to be a comprehensive interest rate risk management policy,<div style="display:inline-block;width:6px;white-space:pre"> </div>which is administered by </div><div id="a24910" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:65px;">management&#8217;s Asset Liability Management<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>Committee (&#8220;ALCO&#8221;).<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>The policy establishes limits of risk, which are quantitative </div><div id="a24913" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:80px;">measures of the percentage change in net interest income (a measure of net<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>interest income at risk) and the fair value of equity capital </div><div id="a24915" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:95px;">(a measure of economic value of equity (&#8220;EVE&#8221;) at risk) resulting from a hypothetical change<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>in interest rates for maturities from one </div><div id="a24918" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:111px;">day to 30 years.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>We measure the potential<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>adverse impacts that changing interest rates may have on our short-term<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>earnings, long-</div><div id="a24924" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:126px;">term value, and liquidity by employing simulation analysis through the use of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>computer modeling.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>The simulation model captures </div><div id="a24927" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:141px;">optionality factors such as call features and interest rate caps and floors<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>embedded in investment and loan portfolio contracts.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>As with </div><div id="a24932" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:157px;">any method of gauging interest rate risk, there are certain shortcomings<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>inherent in the interest rate modeling methodology used by </div><div id="a24934" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:172px;">us.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>When interest rates change, actual movements in different categories<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, loan </div><div id="a24941" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:187px;">prepayments, and withdrawals of time and other deposits, may deviate significantly<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>from assumptions used in the model.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>Finally, the </div><div id="a24944" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:203px;">methodology does not measure or reflect the impact that higher rates may have<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>on adjustable-rate loan clients&#8217; ability to service their </div><div id="a24947" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:218px;">debts, or the impact of rate changes on demand for loan and deposit products. </div><div id="a24950" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:249px;">The statement of financial condition is subject to testing for both parallel and<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>upward and downward shifts in interest rates (assuming </div><div id="a24953" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:264px;">no balance sheet growth) to indicate the inherent interest rate risk. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>prepare a base case (assumes a static rate environment) and </div><div id="a24955" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:279px;">several alternative interest rate simulations for various ranges of upward and downward<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>interest rate changes. This analysis is prepared </div><div id="a24957" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:295px;">quarterly and reported to ALCO, our Market Risk Oversight Committee (&#8220;MROC&#8221;), our<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>Risk Oversight Committee (&#8220;ROC&#8221;) and the </div><div id="a24958" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:310px;">Board of Directors. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>will periodically augment our interest rate simulations with alternative interest<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>rate scenarios that may include </div><div id="a24960" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:325px;">various non-parallel shifts in interest rates, including a flattening or steepening<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>of the yield curve. </div><div id="a24965" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:356px;">Our goal is to structure the statement of financial condition so that net interest earnings at risk over<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>12-month and 24-month periods </div><div id="a24970" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:371px;">and the economic value of equity at risk do not exceed policy guidelines<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>at the various interest rate shock levels. We<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>attempt to </div><div id="a24972" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:387px;">achieve this goal by balancing, within policy limits, the volume of floating-rate<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>liabilities with a similar volume of floating-rate assets, </div><div id="a24977" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:402px;">by keeping the average maturity of fixed-rate asset and liability contracts<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>reasonably matched, by managing the mix of our core </div><div id="a24980" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:417px;">deposits, and by adjusting our rates to market conditions on a continuing<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>basis.<div style="display:inline-block;width:3px;white-space:pre"> </div></div><div id="a24982" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:433px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:48px;white-space:pre"> </div></div><div id="a24984" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-style:italic;left:48px;top:448px;">Analysis.</div><div id="a24985" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;left:97px;top:448px;"><div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div></div><div id="a24986" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:103px;top:448px;">Measures of net interest income at risk produced by simulation analysis are<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>indicators of an institution&#8217;s short-term </div><div id="a24989" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:463px;">performance in alternative rate environments.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px;white-space:pre"> </div>These measures are typically based upon a relatively brief period, and do not </div><div id="a24992" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:479px;">necessarily indicate the long-term prospects or economic value of the institution.<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>The following table presents our net interest income </div><div id="a24997" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:494px;">simulation results for gradual 12-month and 24-month &#8220;ramp&#8221; scenarios<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>applied to the base scenario. The &#8220;ramp&#8221; scenario is a parallel </div><div id="a25002" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:509px;">shift applied gradually over a 12-month period for the million in commitments to extend credit<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>and $7.5 million in standby letters of credit.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div></div><div id="a25847" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:141px;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a client so long as there is no violation of<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>any condition established in the </div><div id="a25850" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:157px;">contract.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>clauses and may require payment of a fee.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>Since </div><div id="a25852" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:172px;">many of the commitments are expected to expire without being drawn upon,<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>the total commitment amounts do not necessarily </div><div id="a25853" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:187px;">represent future cash requirements.<div style="display:inline-block;width:7px;white-space:pre"> </div>Standby letters of credit are conditional commitments issued by us to guarantee<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>the performance </div><div id="a25855" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:203px;">of a client to a third party.<div style="display:inline-block;width:8px;white-space:pre"> </div>We use the same credit<div style="display:inline-block;width:5px;white-space:pre"> </div>policies in establishing commitments and issuing letters of credit as we do for on-</div><div id="a25858" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:218px;">balance sheet instruments. </div><div id="a25861" style="position:absolute;font-family:'Times New Roman';left:48px;top:249px;">If commitments arising from these financial instruments continue to require<div
